Subject: ACME - feature parity & competitive eval follow-up

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and appreciate the candid feedback on where you see gaps vs the hyperscalers. I promised a brief recap and proposed next tests so we can close the parity checklist. Key points from our call: 

- Competitive takeaways: ACME is focused on structured output reliability, streaming function/tool calling behavior, and cost/latency at our target 200QPS load. You flagged: inconsistencies in tool-invocation formatting and streaming deltas from other providers.
- Redwood differentiators we discussed: streaming responses + first-class function/tool calling, configurable structured-output schemas (JSON Schema enforcement), and per-route batching/caching to hit latency SLOs without blowing cost. We also called out our Dedicated option if you need predictable throughput for the tests.

Attachments: I included a competitive matrix (acme-competitive-matrix.pdf) and a short test plan (acme-next-tests-plan.md) with concrete API calls/scripts we recommend. Also attached a small example of streaming tool-call responses (redwood-streaming-examples.txt).

Proposed next tests (we can run these in parallel across teams):
1) Streaming function-call latency: mirror your existing prompts, measure median p50/p95 time-to-first-tool-token and final-tool-token.
2) Structured output validation: run 1k prompts through identical schema and measure validation fail-rate + recovery strategies.
3) Quality parity: side-by-side model responses on the same prompts (fixed seeds where applicable).
4) High-throughput behavior: 200 QPS sustained for 30 minutes to validate batching and Dedicated routing.

Questions / asks for ACME before we run tests:
- Can you share the small sample set you referenced on the call (5–10 canonical prompts + expected JSON schema)? If you can drop that in the Drive link we can consume it directly.
- Do you want us to use Hosted API for the first pass or spin up a short Dedicated pool for the throughput test? We can do both but Dedicated will require a short account-level config (I can loop in our infra team).

Next steps / owners:
- ACME: upload sample prompts + schema to the Drive folder (Liam/Jane) — target by Wed 5/12.
- Redwood: David will share exact API snippets and a small runner script for the tests by Friday 5/14.
- Redwood: I will coordinate scheduling and logistics and book a 30-min sync the week of 5/15 to review initial results.

Thanks — will follow up with David's test runner and the matrix exported after this thread.

Best,

Thanks Jane — quick technical note on the test plan so ACME can align the harness. I attached a tiny runner example in the Drive but pasting the key points here: 

- Streaming function-call behavior: our streaming endpoint sends incremental JSON patches for function arguments as they become available (delta chunks). For tooling parity we recommend measuring two things: time-to-first-arg-token (TTFAT) and time-to-complete-args (TTCA). Some providers only emit a final function payload; we stream deltas so you can begin downstream processing earlier.
- Function calling schema enforcement: Redwood can optionally validate against your JSON Schema server-side and return a validation result alongside the tool-call meta. For the test, we can run with validation enabled and include the validation flag in the response to track fail-rate.
- Structured output / recovery: If a model emits malformed JSON mid-stream, our streaming client returns the best-effort payload and a separate validation error object; we log both. We'll include those logs in the export.
- Throughput considerations: to reach sustained 200 QPS with low p95 latency we recommend a Dedicated pool with 4x gpus of the n1-high variety (we'll propose exact sizes after we see your token distribution). Hosted can run the parity checks but may have variable tail latency.

API snippets: (example)
POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <TEST_TOKEN>
Body: { model: "redwood-stream-1", prompt: "<your prompt>", stream: true, function_schema: { ... } }

We'll provide a small Node runner and a Python runner. I'll drop links in the Drive.

-David
